**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year**

| Year | Film | Award |
|------|------|-------|
| 1998 (21st Japan Academy Prize ceremony) | **Princess Mononoke** (1997) | Picture of the Year |

*Princess Mononoke* was the first Ghibli feature to receive the top honor at the Japan Academy Film Prize, beating out other domestic contenders that year.

---

### How its box‑office success boosted Ghibli’s international popularity

| Aspect | Impact |
|--------|--------|
| **Domestic box‑office record** | The film became the highest‑grossing Japanese animated feature at the time, earning over ¥10 billion (≈US$70 million) in Japan alone. Its commercial triumph proved that Ghibli’s storytelling could command a large audience. |
| **International release** | In 1999, Walt Disney Studios released *Princess Mononoke* in the United States (and later in other territories). It grossed roughly US$30 million worldwide, a remarkable figure for an anime film in the late 1990s. |
| **Critical acclaim abroad** | The film was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature (though the category was created later) and received positive reviews from Western critics, highlighting its mature themes and lush animation. |
| **Distribution ripple effect** | The success convinced major distributors (e.g., Disney, Miramax, later Netflix) to acquire rights to other Ghibli titles. Subsequent releases—*Spirited Away*, *Howl’s Moving Castle*, etc.—were handled by larger international partners, expanding Ghibli’s reach. |
| **Fanbase growth** | The film’s availability on home video, streaming platforms, and in specialty theaters introduced Ghibli’s world‑building and character design to a new generation of viewers outside Japan. This laid the groundwork for a dedicated global fan community. |
| **Industry credibility** | Winning Picture of the Year and achieving strong box‑office returns gave Ghibli leverage in negotiations, allowing the studio to secure better budgets, co‑production deals, and festival slots worldwide. |

In short, *Princess Mononoke*’s domestic blockbuster status, coupled with its successful international release and critical praise, turned Studio Ghibli from a respected Japanese studio into a globally recognized brand. The film’s achievements opened doors for future Ghibli projects, cemented the studio’s reputation for high‑quality animation, and sparked a worldwide fanbase that still thrives today.
